record.original_question: Let G be a random 4-regular graph obtained as the union of two uniformly random cycles on the same vertex set. Let P_G = ∏_{uv∈E(G)} (u-v) be the graph polynomial of G, where the variables correspond to the vertices of G. Is it true that, asymptotically almost surely, the coefficient of the monomial ∏_{v∈V(G)} v^2 in P_G is non-zero?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $V=\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$. Sample independently two uniformly random Hamilton cycles $C_1, C_2$ on the vertex set $V$, and let $G$ be the (multi)graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E(G)=E(C_1)\cup E(C_2)$. Then $G$ is a random $4$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. Associate to each vertex $v\in V$ a formal variable (also denoted $v$), and define the graph polynomial
$$P_G(v_1,\dots,v_n) \;=\; \prod_{uv\in E(G)} (u-v),$$
where each edge contributes one factor with a fixed but arbitrary orientation (the resulting coefficient is determined up to sign). Since $G$ is $4$-regular, $P_G$ is homogeneous of degree $2n$, and the unique monomial of the form $\prod_{v\in V} v^{d_v}$ with all exponents equal is $\prod_{v\in V} v^2$. Let $c_G$ denote the coefficient of $\prod_{v\in V} v^2$ in $P_G$.

Question: Is it true that, as $n\to\infty$, asymptotically almost surely (i.e. with probability tending to $1$) one has $c_G\neq 0$?

Equivalently (by the Alon–Tarsi theorem), is it a.a.s. the case that $G$ admits an Eulerian orientation in which the number of even Eulerian sub-digraphs differs from the number of odd Eulerian sub-digraphs, so that $G$ is $3$-choosable?
artifact.category_tag: Alon-Tarsi number of random regular graphs
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open question at the 33rd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings (2025). Web searches reveal no resolution: known results give the Alon–Tarsi number of specific regular graph families, but the asymptotic almost-sure behavior of the diagonal coefficient of the graph polynomial for the random 4-regular graph (sampled as the union of two random Hamilton cycles) does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Alon-Tarsi Number of Some Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Alon-Tarsi numbers of structured regular graphs; does not address random 4-regular graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on Alon-Tarsi numbers of regular graphs focuses on deterministic families, leaving the random 4-regular case unaddressed.

status_evidence.title: Colorings and Orientations of Graphs (Alon, Tarsi)
status_evidence.snippet: Original Alon-Tarsi theorem connecting nonvanishing of the diagonal coefficient of the graph polynomial to list-colorability.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework underlying the question but no results on random 4-regular graphs.
